newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Hun Sen says Cambodia war over, shelling reported.
newsitem.headline: Hun Sen says Cambodia war over, shelling reported.

text.p: Cambodian co-Prime Minister Hun Sen said on Saturday that the war in his country was over as his rivals had been unable to rally people to their cause, despite reports from northwestern Siem Reap province of shelling in the morning.

Hun Sen, whose forces ousted the democratically elected First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh during two days of fighting in Phnom Penh last weekend, said in his first public appearance since then that his opponents had tried unsuccessfully to seize several provinces.

"On the first day, people wanted to take Battambang, Siem Reap, Preah Vihear, Kompong Thom to create a state within the state," Hun Sen, Cambodia's Second Prime minister, said at a pagoda-opening ceremony about 25 km (15 miles) from Phnom Penh.
"They could not and they were disappointed because the people didn't want to fight, they don't care about war, they only care about their farming," Hun Sen said.
He said his opponents had fled and the Khmer Rouge guerrilla group's hardline leaders, who still hold out in jungle strongholds in the north, would probably be all dead within five years.

Residents in the northwestern town of Siem Reap, capital of the province of the same name, said there was shelling in an area west of the town in the morning. The residents in the town, near the Angkor temple complex about 250 km (150 miles), northwest of Phnom Penh, said the shelling began about an hour after dawn and lasted about 20 minutes.
Ranariddh's forces have been attacking Hun Sen's troops in an attempt to cut off the town, military officials loyal to Hun Sen said on Friday.
The officials declined to comment on whether there had been fighting on Saturday.
Officials of Ranariddh's royalist party have vowed to try to capture territory in the provinces to set up a base for their resistance.
